clinician.final_diagnosis: simultaneous spontaneous bilateral ganglia hemorrhage secondary to uncontrolled hypertension
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 37-year-old man with poorly controlled hypertension presented with sudden severe headache, worsening confusion, right-sided weakness, and mixed aphasia with stupor. Initial non-contrast head CT confirmed simultaneous bilateral basal ganglia hemorrhages (left 5x3cm, right 3x1cm). On admission, blood pressure was critically elevated at 220/120, and laboratory tests including coagulation profile were normal, excluding systemic coagulopathies. Neurological status initially was poor with GCS 8 but improved progressively to 14 by day 10 of hospitalization, consistent with treatment and supportive care. No evidence of vascular malformations was documented, but MRI was ordered without result disclosure. The clinical picture and investigations support spontaneous bilateral ganglia hemorrhage secondary to hypertensive crisis.
